description: Per scene of scripts/fixtures/chrome-png-export.sh, in two tiers compared with excali_raster::diff (a pixel's difference is its largest premultiplied channel difference). The canvas tier (`channel`, `pixels`): at most `pixels` pixels of the whole canvas may differ from Chrome's by more than `channel` levels. The outsideText tier (`outsideText`), required wherever the port draws text: the same over the pixels outside the boxes of the port's text runs (each run's advance, at least an em per character, from 1.25 em above the baseline to 0.5 em below, grown by a quarter em; TextBoxes in tests/chrome_export.rs), so the canvas tier's allowance for glyph edges never reaches the shapes, images and background. Measured on macOS arm64 with the Chromium of tests/web/package-lock.json: the canvas tier of a scene with text allows the pixels measured over 64 levels (32 for the three drawn at a third to a half of the size) plus a quarter and 10; its outsideText tier and the canvas tier of a scene without text allow 8 levels at most, and only the pixels measured over that. A scene with `excluded` is not compared with Chrome (the reason says why): it has no canvas tier, and its outsideText tier holds the pixels outside its text element's box. `note` says where the difference comes from.

default.note: The basic scene's text `export me` (Excalifont, 20 px). Chrome on macOS rasterizes the glyphs through Skia's CoreText path, which smooths (emboldens) the stems; GlyphText fills the same outlines, shaped from the same vendored face and placed on the same baseline, with tiny-skia's analytic coverage. The differences are the edge pixels of the glyphs, a stroke a fraction of a pixel heavier in Chrome. Outside the text boxes the shapes, images and background differ by at most 3 levels.

frames.note: Frame names and embeddable labels are Helvetica, which upstream never ships (`local:`, ADR-004): Chrome draws the machine's Helvetica, the port Liberation Sans (the generic sans-serif a family without faces falls through to), so the label glyphs differ in shape and width: the long name is cut to the frame's width by each font's measurement, `A frame n...` in Chrome and `A frame na...` in the port. Outside the text boxes the shapes, images and background differ by at most 1 levels.

smiley_embedded_v2.note: The scene is one text element, the emoji U+1F600 in Virgil.
